blocks.content: Quiz: Why do we use setEntries([...entries, newEntry]) instead of entries.push(newEntry) and setEntries(entries)?
Tap an option below to answer:
React needs to receive a new array to notice the change and update the screen
When you pass the same array back, React sees nothing different and skips the re-render.
When you pass the same array back, React sees nothing different and skips the re-render.
push() is not allowed in React
push() works fine in JavaScript. The problem is that it changes the original array instead of creating a new one.
push() works fine in JavaScript. The problem is that it changes the original array instead of creating a new one.
Spread syntax runs faster than push()
Speed is not the reason; it's about how React spots changes, not performance.
Speed is not the reason; it's about how React spots changes, not performance.
So we can sort the entries later
Sorting has nothing to do with it. React just needs a fresh array each time state updates.
